candidates.title: Exposed Directory Listing - /ftp/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Directory listing exposes: acquisitions.md, announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package-lock.json.bak, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml. Path traversal via %2500.md null-byte bypass confirmed working to download non-.md files (package.json.bak, encrypt.pyc, coupons_2013.md.bak).
candidates.causality: Server configured with directory listing enabled for /ftp/ path with .md extension restriction bypassable via null-byte injection.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /ftp/ returns HTML directory listing. GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returns 200 with file contents.
candidates.impact: Sensitive files exposed including encrypted announcements, password-protected kdbx file, source backups, error logs. Path traversal enables reading arbitrary files.

candidates.title: Exposed Directory Listing - /encryptionkeys/
candidates.proof_excerpt: Directory listing exposes jwt.pub (RSA public key) and premium.key (value: 1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42). jwt.pub used for JWT key confusion attack.
candidates.causality: Server configured with directory listing enabled.
candidates.impact: JWT public key exposed enables JWT signature verification bypass via key confusion.

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure - /api/Challenges
candidates.proof_excerpt: Full challenge list accessible without authentication, revealing challenge solutions status, descriptions, difficulty ratings, and source code hints
candidates.impact: Exposes internal challenge metadata including mitigation URLs and solution hints

candidates.title: Admin Login Credentials - Weak Password
candidates.proof_excerpt: Admin account admin@juice-sh.op authenticated successfully with password 'admin123'
candidates.reproducibility: POST /rest/user/login with {"email":"admin@juice-sh.op","password":"admin123"} returns valid JWT token
candidates.impact: Full administrative access to application including user list, basket contents, order history, and application configuration

candidates.title: SQL Injection Authentication Bypass
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /rest/user/login with {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"wrong"} returns valid JWT for admin user (id:1, admin@juice-sh.op, role:admin). The SQL injection payload bypasses authentication entirely, allowing login as any user without valid credentials. Response: {"authentication":{"token":"eyJ..."},"bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}
candidates.causality: The login endpoint concatenates user input directly into SQL query without parameterization. The payload ' OR 1=1-- closes the WHERE clause comparison and comments out the remainder, causing the query to return the first user row regardless of password.
candidates.reproducibility: Send POST /rest/user/login with Content-Type: application/json and body {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"wrong"}. Server returns 200 with admin JWT token.
candidates.impact: Complete authentication bypass allows attacker to impersonate any user (including admin) without knowing credentials. Full application compromise including access to all user data, orders, basket contents, and application configuration.
candidates.precondition: None - endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication

candidates.title: Mass Assignment Privilege Escalation
candidates.proof_excerpt: POST /api/Users with {"email":"hacker@test.com","password":"test123","securityAnswer":"test","securityQuestion":"Your favorite test?","role":"admin"} creates user id=26 with role="admin". Response: {"status":"success","data":{"id":26,"email":"hacker@test.com","role":"admin","isActive":true,...}}
candidates.causality: The user registration endpoint accepts and persists the 'role' field from the request body without filtering. This allows a registering user to set their own privilege level.
candidates.reproducibility: Send POST /api/Users with Content-Type: application/json and body containing "role":"admin". Server returns 201 Created with user having admin role.
candidates.impact: Any attacker can register as an administrator, gaining full privileges over the application including access to user management, order processing, and configuration.
candidates.precondition: None - endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication

candidates.title: Unauthenticated Secret Disclosure - User Password Hashes
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/memories/ as anonymous (no JWT, no cookies) returns all user records including password hashes (MD5). Exposed data includes: bjoern@owasp.org:9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466 (deluxe), bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com:6edd9d726cbdc873c539e41ae8757b8c (admin), ethereum@juice-sh.op:2c17c6393771ee3048ae34d6b380c5ec (deluxe), john@juice-sh.op:00479e957b6b42c459ee5746478e4d45 (customer), emma@juice-sh.op:402f1c4a75e316afec5a6ea63147f739 (customer). Also exposes deluxeToken values for deluxe users.
candidates.causality: The /rest/memories/ endpoint returns User objects with nested user data including sensitive fields (password, deluxeToken, totpSecret) without requiring authentication. The eager-loading of User associations includes these sensitive fields.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /rest/memories/ with no authentication headers. Server returns 200 with full user objects including password hashes and deluxe tokens.
candidates.impact: All user password hashes are exposed to unauthenticated attackers. These MD5 hashes can be easily cracked offline, leading to account takeover for all users including administrators (bjoern.kimminich@gmail.com) and deluxe users. Deluxe tokens enable access to premium features.
candidates.precondition: None - endpoint is publicly accessible without any authentication

candidates.title: Excessive Data Exposure - Admin Application Configuration
candidates.proof_excerpt: Endpoint returns full application configuration without authentication including: Google OAuth client ID (1005568560502-6hm16lef8oh46hr2d98vf2ohlnj4nfhq.apps.googleusercontent.com), authorized OAuth redirect URIs, chatbot model (gemma4:e4b), social media URLs, challenge configuration, product catalog with pricing, and internal server configuration.
candidates.causality: Admin-only configuration endpoint lacks access control checks.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration returns 200 with full config JSON regardless of authentication state.
candidates.impact: Exposes sensitive configuration including OAuth client credentials, internal URLs, LLM model details, and product pricing data that could aid further attacks.

candidates.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion - alg:none Accepted
candidates.proof_excerpt: JWT with alg:'none' (no signature) accepted by server. GET /rest/user/whoami with Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiAibm9uZSIsICJ0eXAiOiAiSldUIn0.<payload>. returns 200 with user data {user:{id:1,email:'admin@juice-sh.op'}} confirming admin-level authentication. GET /rest/admin/application-configuration with same token returns 200 with full application config including Google OAuth clientId, LLM model, and product pricing.
candidates.causality: JWT verification library allows 'none' algorithm. The server does not enforce a whitelist of allowed signing algorithms, enabling attackers to bypass signature verification entirely.
candidates.reproducibility: 1. Encode header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} in base64url. 2. Encode arbitrary payload with desired claims. 3. Send token without signature (trailing dot). Server returns 200 with authenticated user context.
candidates.impact: Complete authentication bypass. Attacker can forge arbitrary JWT tokens to impersonate any user, including administrators, without knowing the signing key. Full application compromise.
candidates.precondition: None - attack performed from unauthenticated state using public endpoint

candidates.title: JWT Key Confusion - HS256 Signed with Public RSA Key
candidates.proof_excerpt: JWT with HS256 algorithm signed using the RSA public key (from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub) as HMAC secret accepted by server. GET /rest/user/whoami with forged token returns 200 {user:{id:1,email:'admin@juice-sh.op'}}. The public key retrieved from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (-----BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY-----MIGJAoGBAM3CosR73CBNcJsLv5E90NsFt6qN1uziQ484gbOoule8leXHFbyIzPQRozgEpSpiwhr6d2/c0CfZHEJ3m5tV0klxfjfM7oqjRMURnH/rmBjcETQ7qzIISZQ/iptJ3p7Gi78X5ZMhLNtDkUFU9WaGdiEb+SnC39wjErmJSfmGb7i1AgMBAAE=) was used as HMAC-SHA256 secret to sign the forged token.
candidates.causality: JWT library is configured to accept RS256 tokens but does not validate the algorithm against an expected value. When an attacker presents a token with alg:'HS256' and signs it with the public RSA key (which is publicly accessible), the server uses the public key as an HMAC secret, verifying the forged signature as valid.
candidates.reproducibility: 1. Retrieve public RSA key from GET /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub. 2. Create JWT header {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}. 3. Create admin payload. 4. Sign HMAC-SHA256 using public key content as secret. 5. Server accepts the forged token as valid admin authentication.
candidates.impact: Complete authentication bypass. Any attacker with access to the public RSA key (exposed in /encryptionkeys/) can forge arbitrary valid JWT tokens for any user, including administrators. Full application compromise.
candidates.precondition: Retrieve RSA public key from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (unauthenticated directory listing)

candidates.title: Login Differential Behavior Confirmed
candidates.proof_excerpt: Valid login (admin@juice-sh.op/admin123) returns HTTP 200 with JWT token. Invalid login (wrong password) returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized. Login differential is consistent.
candidates.causality: Standard authentication logic with different response codes for valid vs invalid credentials.
candidates.reproducibility: POST valid credentials → 200 + JWT. POST invalid credentials → 401.
candidates.impact: Information disclosure about valid usernames through response code differential.

candidates.title: 2FA Surface Mapped - TOTP Secret Exposed
candidates.proof_excerpt: GET /rest/2fa/status as authenticated admin returns {"setup":false,"secret":"3DHNAHMZPWO43K74NZGOYCOAJSDSTTKX","email":"admin@juice-sh.op","setupToken":"eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9.eyJzZWNyZXQiOiIzREhOQUhNWlBXTzQzSzc0TlpHT1lDT0FKU0RTVFRLWCIsInR5cGUiOiJ0b3RwX3NldHVwX3NlY3JldCIsImlhdCI6MTc4NDg0NjYzMH0..."}. TOTP secret and setupToken are exposed.
candidates.causality: 2FA status endpoint returns TOTP secret in response, enabling potential 2FA setup bypass.
candidates.reproducibility: GET /rest/2fa/status with valid JWT token. Server returns TOTP secret in response body.
candidates.impact: Exposed TOTP secret enables attacker to set up 2FA on victim account or bypass existing 2FA if weak implementation.

Re-tested actionable priors and proved 3 high-severity vulnerabilities with live evidence: (1) SQL injection authentication bypass on /rest/user/login using ' OR 1=1-- logs in as admin without credentials; (2) Mass assignment privilege escalation via POST /api/Users with role=admin creates admin account; (3) Unauthenticated secret-grade disclosure at /rest/memories/ leaking all user password hashes (MD5) and deluxe tokens.
